---
title: Account Risk
engine: markdown
---

An account model can answer questions at different levels: which recent payments
will be disputed, and how much the account will lose over the next month.
This advanced example combines repeated targets with an account-level target.
Start with [Add Transaction History](../tutorials/transaction-history.qmd)
for a single payment prediction.

## One Observation

```yaml
account_id: account-42
account_age_days: 420
recent_transactions:
  - days_ago: 3
    amount: 86.50
    merchant: grocery
    line_items:
      - sku: basket-17
        quantity: 2
      - sku: basket-03
        quantity: 1
    disputed_next_30_days: false
loss_next_30_days: 0.0
```

One record describes an account at a decision time. Transactions and line items
contain only information available then. Both labels describe the following
30 days: a dispute for each listed transaction, and total account loss in the
application's common currency. Define the outcome window and loss attribution
before creating training and held-out records.

## Place Each Target With Its Subject

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.md(
    account_age_days=rf.Number,
    recent_transactions=rf.Branch(
        length=64,
        overflow="tail",
        days_ago=rf.Number,
        amount=rf.Number,
        merchant=rf.Category,
        line_items=rf.Branch(
            length=16,
            sku=rf.Category,
            quantity=rf.Number,
        ),
        disputed_next_30_days=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
    ),
    loss_next_30_days=rf.Number(mask=True),
)
```

```{typst}
    )),
    node("disputed_next_30_days", width: 175pt, kind: "target", type: "Boolean", detail: "per transaction"),

)))
```

Line items form context within each transaction. The transaction history then
sends its reduced representation to the account root. Each dispute decoder
uses its ancestor context and aligned visible siblings; its output retains the
transaction coordinates. See [Model Tree](../core-concepts/model-tree.qmd).

Both targets use `mask=True`. Their labels supply supervision and are excluded
from input embedding. At prediction time, omit `loss_next_30_days` and omit
`disputed_next_30_days` from each transaction. Keep the transaction records:
they define the repeated positions to predict.

## Preserve The Context The Task Needs

The `md` preset uses Attention reductions with four summaries per parent
coordinate. Those summaries bound the context sent upward; they are not one
token per original line item. If matching a SKU across transactions matters,
represent the shared relationship through aligned input or preprocessing.
Nesting does not join database tables.

`overflow="tail"` assumes transactions are sorted oldest to newest. The line
items keep the default first-items policy. Choose both capacities from the
records the application needs to model.

## Evaluate The Two Outcomes

Fit using [data modules](../guides/data-modules.qmd) and
[Training And Checkpoints](../guides/lightning.qmd). Hold out later decision
windows and control overlap between related account snapshots.

Inspect dispute ranking and calibration separately from account-loss errors.
Their combined validation loss can hide a regression in one target. This
example specifies a model design; it makes no claim about measured quality.

Results are under
`predictions.recent_transactions[i].disputed_next_30_days` and
`predictions.loss_next_30_days`. Retain `account_id` and the application's
transaction identifiers when joining outputs back to records. Account for the retained
history window: an attention summary is not a transaction identifier.
See [Prediction Output](../guides/prediction-output.qmd).
